findings.description: The bucket is explicitly noted as public with no ACL restriction defined, allowing unauthenticated or unauthorized users to read or write objects such as customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket (including customer-master.xlsx) are not encrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, so accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of objects cannot be recovered, and combined with public access this increases risk of data loss or tampering.
A sensitive file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing customer data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted despite logging and versioning being configured.
